title: Speeding Up Search for Significant Truncated Differentials
summary: Existing surrogate differentiation techniques support black-box analysis of 64-bit cryptosystems, but whether similar methods can speed the search for significant truncated differentials remains open.

formal_statement.body: Surrogate differentiation techniques used to detect high-probability statistical properties of cryptosystems apply to black-box functions and are fast enough to analyze 64-bit cryptosystems; the unresolved task is to determine whether similar techniques can reduce the search complexity for significant truncated differentials.

scope.domain: This is a symmetric cryptanalysis problem about truncated differentials and efficient search.
parameters: 64-bit cryptosystems — size scope of the reported analysis
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether similar techniques can speed up the search for significant truncated differentials.

citations.label: Efficient Detection of High Probability Statistical Properties of Cryptosystems via Surrogate Differentiation

progress.summary: Section 5 presents this as an open problem following the paper's black-box statistical cryptanalysis algorithms. It asks whether similar techniques can speed up the search for significant truncated differentials.
